You can track issues and tasks here: GitHub Project Board: View on GitHub 1.1 Introduction 1.1.1 Purpose 1.2 Required Information 1.2.1 Datasets This tutorial uses the following publicly available datasets: Data Provider Dataset Type Natural Resources Canada (CFS / CWFIS) National Burned Area Composite (NBAC) wildfire perimeters (1972–2024) ([cwfis.cfs.nrcan.gc.ca](https://cwfis.cfs.nrcan.gc.ca/datamart/metadata/nbac?utm_source=chatgpt.com “NBAC - Canadian Wildland Fire Information System Metadata”)) Natural Resources Canada (EGS) Floods in Canada – Archive (flood extent products) (open.canada.ca) Polygon (vector) Environment and Climate Change Canada Historical climate observations & station metadata (climate.weather.gc.ca) Point + time series   This tutorial also uses datasets with access restrictions. Access may require institutional access, and/or data-use agreements. Data Provider Dataset Access Statistics Canada Postal Code Conversion File (PCCF) v8B Licensed Canadian Urban Environmental Health Research Consortium (CANUE) Local Climate Zones & PM2.5 (smoke) by Postcode Request via project creation in CANUE (free) 1.2.2 R packages The following R packages are required to run the code in this book: Data processing and wrangling dplyr tidyverse tidyr lubridate data.table tibble readr purrr stringr readxl writexl Data visualization and mapping ggplot2 maps Spatial analysis sf geosphere Data download weathercan Optional furrr (offers improved processing speeds) The following code installs (if needed) and loads these packages: # Vector of required packages packages <- c( "dplyr", "tidyr", "lubridate", "data.table", "tibble", "readr", "purrr", "stringr", "readxl", "writexl", "ggplot2", "maps", "sf", "geosphere", "weathercan", "furrr", "tidyverse" ) # Install any that are missing installed <- rownames(installed.packages()) to_install <- setdiff(packages, installed) if (length(to_install) > 0) { install.packages(to_install) } # Load all packages invisible(lapply(packages, library, character.only = TRUE)) ##
